intro: I’m Anand Grandhi. Previously at Amazon (L6), I led product initiatives and learning operations, working across customer experience, personalisation and operational transformation.
Today, at ARCHMATION, I bring that experience to AI product strategy, intelligent workflows and business automation.
Earlier, at BYJU’S, I worked on interactive learning products at scale.

projects.title: Using AI to take a six-hour workflow down to 45 minutes
projects.problem: Publishing a single article meant researching, drafting, reviewing and moving information between multiple tools. The production process was consuming hours of skilled team time.
projects.discovery: Writing was only one part of the problem; coordination and repetitive handoffs were also consuming time.
projects.decision: Rather than simply introducing an AI writer, I designed a workflow around the entire production process.
projects.approach: I defined an AI-assisted research and content pipeline using structured inputs, automation and editorial review, connecting research, drafting and publishing.
projects.outcome: Reported production time fell from 6.5 hours to 45 minutes per article.
projects.assurance: Human editorial review remained part of the workflow. The time-saving figure is a reported project outcome.

projects.title: Turning a declining product into a daily user habit
projects.problem: Despite a substantial learning content library, Daily Digest was losing users. Daily active users had fallen from 50,000 to 35,000, and repeat engagement was weakening.
projects.discovery: I identified the decline using engagement and retention data. A large library alone was not enough to create a compelling reason to return every day.
projects.decision: I proposed short, personalised learning sessions with clear next actions, rather than presenting students with more content.
projects.approach: I defined the core experience and personalisation logic, working with product, design, research and engineering teams through discussions and reviews. Leadership approved the direction.
projects.outcome: Reported DAU grew to over 80,000 after the revamp. Session duration increased by 64% and retention by 32%.
projects.assurance: I monitored engagement and retention after launch and used the data to decide subsequent improvements.

projects.title: Making institutional knowledge actionable with AI
projects.problem: Counsellors work with information scattered across conversations, historical records and student planning documents. Valuable institutional knowledge is difficult to reuse consistently.
projects.discovery: The opportunity is not merely to summarise meetings, but to connect evidence from conversations with structured records and actionable planning.
projects.decision: I designed three interconnected concepts: transcript intelligence, an intelligent counsellor workbook and a personalised student planning engine.
projects.approach: I developed the product and workflow concepts alongside an AI-assisted reference implementation, focusing on structured extraction, traceable evidence and human review.
projects.outcome: The reference prototype demonstrated elements of extraction, planning and validation. Production adoption and business impact are not claimed.
projects.assurance: Evidence validation, contradiction handling and approval were included in the reference implementation. Live inference and broader knowledge retrieval require further verification.

projects.title: Building a trustworthy AI workflow for customer acquisition
projects.problem: Early-stage growth teams need to research potential customers, qualify opportunities and coordinate follow-up without losing track of evidence or decisions.
projects.discovery: Automating activity alone is not enough: unverified claims and premature funnel-stage changes can create unreliable growth reporting.
projects.decision: I focused on separating account research, validation and qualification, with explicit rules for when an action or stage transition is allowed.
projects.approach: I explored a multi-agent workflow and an AI-assisted reference system for structured research, evidence-based qualification and controlled operations.
projects.outcome: A reference run demonstrated a citation rejection and correction loop. The prototype test suite and dry run demonstrated approval and evidence controls; commercial growth outcomes are not claimed.
projects.assurance: Human approval gates, deterministic checks and evidence-based stage transitions were central to the design.

projects.title: Publishing faster without sacrificing editorial accuracy
projects.problem: Repeated reviews slowed the release of learning content and created avoidable coordination across subject experts and editorial teams.
projects.discovery: The process needed clearer quality criteria and fewer avoidable review loops, rather than simply asking teams to work faster.
projects.decision: I focused on standardising quality expectations and improving the review workflow.
projects.approach: I worked on editorial operating processes, review criteria and production coordination across teams.
projects.outcome: Reported publishing turnaround decreased by 40%, accuracy reached 98%, and review rounds fell from eight to three.
projects.assurance: Quality and turnaround were monitored together so speed would not become the only success measure.

projects.title: Scaling interactive STEM experiences across a curriculum
projects.problem: Interactive learning requires subject expertise, design, art, software development and production to work together. Building every experience independently makes scale difficult.
projects.discovery: The challenge was as much about coordinating specialist teams and reusable learning patterns as it was about creating individual experiences.
projects.decision: I focused on learning objectives and repeatable interactive experience patterns that teams could execute at scale.
projects.approach: I worked across pedagogy, design, development and production to deliver interactive STEM experiences.
projects.outcome: The initiative delivered more than 300 applets and 150 games.
projects.assurance: Learning objectives and subject-matter review formed part of the content development approach.

projects.title: Removing friction from the student doubt-resolution journey
projects.problem: Students encountering a difficult question needed a way to get help without losing momentum in their learning journey.
projects.discovery: Doubt resolution needed to be treated as a product experience, not simply a support activity.
projects.decision: I defined the core behaviour and user journey for doubt resolution, connecting help with the learning experience.
projects.approach: I contributed to the launch of doubt on chat and its integration with the help centre, working across product and operations.
projects.outcome: The service handled more than 50,000 queries in its first three months.
projects.assurance: The volume demonstrates usage, not a verified resolution-quality or satisfaction score.

projects.title: Helping teachers see where students were actually struggling
projects.problem: Assessment data could show which students scored poorly, but teachers also needed to understand what concepts and misconceptions were driving those scores.
projects.discovery: A raw score is less actionable than a view of concept-level gaps and cohort patterns.
projects.decision: I focused on translating student assessment and engagement data into instructional priorities.
projects.approach: I worked on teacher insight concepts using knowledge-graph mappings, assessment results and misconception patterns to support lesson preparation.
projects.outcome: The approach supported more targeted instructional planning. A quantified impact figure is not available here.
projects.assurance: The design relied on concept mappings and assessment evidence rather than unsupported inferences.

projects.title: Turning fragmented content into structured knowledge
projects.problem: Large learning libraries are difficult to personalise when content lacks a shared map of concepts and prerequisites.
projects.discovery: A structured representation of learning objectives can connect content, assessment, remediation and progression.
projects.decision: I focused on defining testable learning objectives and their relationships, including prerequisites and misconception mappings.
projects.approach: I worked on knowledge-graph structures and content tagging across curricula to support learning pathways.
projects.outcome: The structures enabled more systematic content discovery and pathway design.
projects.assurance: Subject-matter expertise and content mapping were foundational to the approach.
